- If sentiment is negative in the recent history (especially >3 days), reduce forecast slope or shift mean downward to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast momentum in next 5–7 days.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often overestimates recovery — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent low.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive but price history shows volatility, model tends to over-forecast upward — apply a 2–3% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near-term decline after a peak — adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in true price drop.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple small negative signals (e.g., -0.20 repeated), model tends to ignore them — apply a 5–10% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
